speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify the timeline: did your rash appear before or after you started feeling feverish, runny nose, and headache? Additionally, can you describe the appearance of the rash—does it look like small red spots, hives, or a measles-like pattern?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: That description of a "measles-like" rash appearing on the face first and sparing the mouth is very specific; did you notice any swelling around your joints or excessive drooling when the rash appeared? Additionally, please tell me if you have had any recent exposure to a child with a similar rash or if you were recently vaccinated.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19. The combination of a "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area, followed by a lacy or pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, along with mild flu-like symptoms, is classic for this condition.
